requirements.title: Per-run record lists
requirements.rationale: A developer debugging an agent needs the records of one run, in order and filtered, without seeing another run's or another workspace's data.

criteria.condition: a caller with read access to the workspace, whose credential is an API key, the admin token or a PAT holding `audit:read` or `audit:write`, sends `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/runs/:run_id/events`, `…/sessions/outcomes`, `…/tools/calls`, `…/tools/errors` or `…/traces`, on a workspace of any status
criteria.action: answer the records of that kind stored for the workspace and run of the path, and no record of another run or another workspace, each with every field of its record, ordered by (`timestamp`, `id`) ascending
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{"items": [...], "next_cursor": string or null}`; a run event item has `id`, `workspace`, `run_id`, `timestamp`, `ingested_at`, `event_type`, `severity`, `node_id`, `session_id`, `payload`; a run without records answers `items: []` and `next_cursor: null`

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()

workspaces ws1 (later archived in the archived case) and ws2; for each record kind three records under (ws1, run A), one under (ws1, run B) and one under (ws2, run A), written through the telemetry store of package 50
check.pseudocode: in internal/telemetry/read_test.go, a table over the five list routes x workspace {ready, archived} x credential {owner API key, org member API key, PAT with audit:read, PAT with only audit:write, admin token}: r = get(route for run A on ws1, cred); assert r.status == 200; assert ids(r.items) == the three ids seeded for (ws1, run A) sorted by (timestamp, id), where two records share a timestamp and differ in id; assert every item has every field of its record kind and JSON-valued fields are JSON values, not strings; assert no id of (ws1, run B) or (ws2, run A) appears; assert get(route for a well-formed run id with no records).json == {items: [], next_cursor: null}

criteria.condition: a per-run list route is called with `order=desc`, or with `limit` and the `cursor` of the previous page
criteria.action: reverse the order to (`timestamp`, `id`) descending for `order=desc`, and page through the list in the requested order without repeating or skipping a record
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; following `next_cursor` from the first page until it is null yields every record of the run exactly once in the requested order; `next_cursor` is null on the last page

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
five records of each kind under one run, two of them with the same timestamp
check.pseudocode: in internal/telemetry/read_test.go, a table over the five list routes x order {asc, desc}: all = get(route?order=o).items; pages = follow(route?order=o&limit=2) until next_cursor == null; assert concat(pages) == all; assert all for desc == reverse(all for asc); assert len(pages) == 3 and the last page has next_cursor null

criteria.condition: a per-run list route is called with one or more of its filters (`event_type`, `severity`, `node_id`, `session_id` on events; `node_id`, `session_id`, `status` on outcomes; `node_id`, `session_id`, `tool_name` on tool calls and tool errors; `event_type`, `node_id`, `session_id` on traces) or with `since` or `until`
criteria.action: return only the records that equal every given filter value exactly and whose `timestamp` is at or after `since` and before `until`
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the matching records only; a record whose `timestamp` equals `since` is included and one whose `timestamp` equals `until` is excluded

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
records of each kind at timestamps T1 < T2 < T3 with differing node_id, session_id, severity, status, tool_name and event_type
check.pseudocode: in internal/telemetry/read_test.go, a table of {route, query, expected ids} with one row per filter of each route, one row combining two filters, one row with a filter value that is a prefix of a stored value (expects no match), and rows since=T2 (expects T2 and T3), until=T2 (expects T1), since=T1&until=T3 (expects T1 and T2), since given with a +02:00 offset equal to T2: assert ids(get(route+query).items) == expected

criteria.condition: a per-run list route is called by a caller with read access with a `run_id` that is not `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_` followed by six lower-case hexadecimal digits, a `severity` outside `info`, `warning`, `error`, `critical`, an `order` outside `asc`, `desc`, on the traces route an `event_type` outside `session.init`, `assistant.message`, `tool.use`, `tool.error`, `session.result`, a `session_id` that is not a UUID, a `since` or `until` that is not RFC 3339, a `since` that is not before `until`, a `limit` outside 1 to 200, or a cursor that is malformed or was issued for another query
criteria.action: refuse the request without reading any record
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` and a message that names the offending parameter

setup: the read handlers mounted on an httptest server with a telemetry store wrapped by a call recorder
a caller with read access
check.pseudocode: in internal/telemetry/read_test.go, a table of {route, path run_id, query, parameter name}: run_id '2026', run_id '20260601_120000_ABCDEF', run_id '20260601_120000_abcde'; severity=fatal; order=up; traces event_type=tool.call; session_id=abc; since=yesterday; until=2026-06-01; since=T&until=T; since later than until; limit=0; limit=201; limit=x; cursor=%%%; a cursor taken from the events route sent to the traces route; a cursor taken with node_id=a sent with node_id=b: r = get(route+query); assert r.status == 400 and r.error_type == 'invalid_request' and r.message contains the parameter name; assert the store saw no read

criteria.condition: one of the seven per-run read routes (the five lists, `…/postmortem`, `…/transcript`) is called without a valid credential, with a PAT that holds neither `audit:read` nor `audit:write`, or by a caller who has no read access to the workspace
criteria.action: refuse the request and return no telemetry
criteria.contract: no valid credential: HTTP 401 with `error_type` `unauthenticated`; PAT without the scope: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`, for an existing and for a missing workspace alike; no read access or a slug that does not exist: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found`

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
workspace ws1 with telemetry and a user `outsider` who is neither its owner nor a member of its organization
check.pseudocode: in internal/telemetry/read_test.go, a table over the seven per-run read routes: assert get(route, no credential).status == 401 and error_type == 'unauthenticated'; p = PAT with scope sessions:read only; assert get(route on ws1, p).status == 403 and error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert get(route on 'nope', p).status == 403; a = get(route on ws1, outsider key); b = get(route on 'nope', outsider key); assert a.status == 404 and a.error_type == 'not_found' and a.body == b.body

requirements.title: Postmortem and transcript of a run
requirements.rationale: The postmortem says why a run stopped and the transcript shows what one node said and did; both are read far more often than they are written.

criteria.condition: a caller with read access sends `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/runs/:run_id/postmortem` and the run has a postmortem in this workspace
criteria.action: answer the stored postmortem with every field
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `id`, `workspace`, `run_id`, `timestamp`, `ingested_at`, `schema_version`, `run_status`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `task_summary`, `cost_summary`, `blocked_tasks`, `session_history`; `task_summary` and `cost_summary` are JSON objects and `blocked_tasks` and `session_history` JSON arrays

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
workspace ws1 with a postmortem for run A whose task_summary is {total: 4} and whose blocked_tasks is []
check.pseudocode: in internal/telemetry/postmortem_read_test.go: r = get('/api/v1/workspaces/ws1/runs/'+runA+'/postmortem', owner key); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json equals the stored postmortem field by field; assert r.json.task_summary.total == 4 and r.json.blocked_tasks is an array

criteria.condition: the postmortem route is called by a caller with read access for a run that has no postmortem in this workspace, including a run whose postmortem exists only in another workspace
criteria.action: refuse the read
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `postmortem_not_found`

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
workspaces ws1 and ws2 readable by the caller; a postmortem for run A in ws1 only
check.pseudocode: in internal/telemetry/postmortem_read_test.go, a table over {a run with records and no postmortem, a run id nothing was stored for, run A read through ws2 while its postmortem is in ws1}: r = get(postmortem route); assert r.status == 404 and r.error_type == 'postmortem_not_found'

criteria.condition: a caller with read access sends `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/runs/:run_id/transcript?node_id=N`
criteria.action: take the trace records of that workspace, run and node ordered by `timestamp`, then `sequence`, skip every `session.result`, and turn each remaining trace into one item whose `role` is `system` for `session.init`, `assistant` for `assistant.message`, `tool_use` for `tool.use` and `tool_error` for `tool.error`, whose `content` is `data.content` when that is a string and `""` otherwise, and whose `tool_name` is `data.tool_name` when that is a string and null otherwise
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{"run_id", "node_id", "items": [{"role", "content", "tool_name", "timestamp"}], "next_cursor"}`

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()

traces of (ws1, run A, node n1): session.init, assistant.message, tool.use and tool.error (same timestamp, sequences 2 and 1 stored in that order), assistant.message, session.result; one trace of node n2
check.pseudocode: in internal/telemetry/transcript_test.go: r = get(transcript route for run A, node_id=n1); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.run_id == runA and r.json.node_id == 'n1'; assert roles(r.items) == ['system', 'assistant', 'tool_use', 'tool_error', 'assistant']; assert the two traces sharing a timestamp appear in sequence order 1 then 2; assert the item built from data {content: 'hi'} has content 'hi' and tool_name null; the one from data {content: {a: 1}, tool_name: 'bash'} has content '' and tool_name 'bash'; the one from data {tool_name: 7} has tool_name null; the one from data null has content ''; assert no item for session.result and no item of node n2; assert each item has exactly the keys role, content, tool_name, timestamp

criteria.condition: the transcript route is called with `limit` and `cursor`, or for a run or node nothing is stored for
criteria.action: page through the transcript items in order without repeating or skipping one, and answer an empty list for an unknown run or node
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; pages joined equal the unpaged transcript; an unknown run or node answers `items: []` with `next_cursor: null`

the traces of the transcript check above, with the session.result in the middle of the sequence so that a page boundary falls on it

criteria.condition: the transcript route is called without `node_id` or with an empty one, or the postmortem or transcript route is called with a `run_id` that does not match the run id format, or the transcript route with a `limit` outside 1 to 200 or a malformed cursor
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` and a message that names `node_id`, `run_id`, `limit` or `cursor`

requirements.title: One audit query over hub events and run events
requirements.rationale: An operator reconstructing who did what needs the hub's own events and the agents' events in one list, newest first.

criteria.condition: a caller whose credential is an API key, the admin token or a PAT holding `audit:read` or `audit:write` sends `GET /api/v1/audit`
criteria.action: answer one list that merges the hub events and the run events the caller may see, ordered by time descending, then `id` descending, where the time of a hub event is its `time` and the time of a run event its `timestamp`
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{"items": [...], "next_cursor": string or null}`; with nothing to return `items` is `[]`

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()

workspace ws1; three hub events written through the event component of package 52 and three run events written through the telemetry store, with interleaved times; one hub event and one run event share the same second
check.pseudocode: in internal/audit/query_test.go: r = get('/api/v1/audit', admin token); assert r.status == 200; assert [(i.source, i.id) for i in r.items] == the six seeded records sorted by (time desc, id desc), in which hub and agent items interleave and two items share a time and are ordered by id descending; on an empty hub assert r.json == {items: [], next_cursor: null}; repeat with a PAT holding only audit:write and assert status 200

criteria.action: for any item of the audit list, return exactly the members `source`, `id`, `type`, `time`, `workspace`, `session_id`, `seq`, `actor_type`, `actor_id`, `resource_type`, `resource_id`, `action`, `metadata`, `run_id`, `node_id`, `severity` and `payload`; set `source` `hub` and the hub event record's values for a hub event with the four agent members null; set `source` `agent`, `type` to the run event's `event_type`, `time` to its `timestamp` with fractional seconds, and `run_id`, `node_id`, `severity`, `payload` for a run event with the seven hub members null
criteria.contract: every item is a JSON object with those seventeen keys; `metadata` and `payload` are JSON objects or null, never strings

criteria.condition: `GET /api/v1/audit` is called with `limit` and with the `cursor` of the previous page
criteria.action: page through the merged list across both sources without repeating or skipping an item that existed throughout
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; the pages joined equal the unpaged list; `next_cursor` is null on the last page, also when the number of items is a multiple of `limit`

the six records of the merge check

criteria.condition: the caller is not an admin token
criteria.action: return only the hub events the visibility rule of the event component lets the caller see and only the run events of workspaces the caller can read, and for a workspace-bound token only records of the workspaces its binding covers and no hub event without a workspace
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; a record the caller may not see is absent from every page; the admin token receives every stored record, including those of a workspace that no longer exists

requirements.title: Audit filters and their validation
requirements.rationale: A filter that is silently ignored or quietly returns nothing makes an audit answer untrustworthy; every filter either narrows the result or is refused.

criteria.condition: `GET /api/v1/audit` is called with `source`, `workspace`, `types` or `session_id`
criteria.action: apply each given filter to both sources and combine them with AND: `source` keeps one source; `workspace` matches the slug exactly; `types` is a comma-separated list whose entries combine with OR, each an exact type or a prefix ending in `*`, matched against a hub event's `type` and a run event's `event_type`; `session_id` matches exactly, in any letter case
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the matching items; a type that no record has gives `items: []`, not an error; `types=*` matches every record

workspace ws1 and its fork ws1--f1; hub events of types parley.change.land, parley.change.open and parley.workspace.sync; run events of types tool.started and session.fail; some records carry session id S
check.pseudocode: in internal/audit/filters_test.go, a table of {query, expected ids}: source=hub; source=agent; workspace=ws1 (ws1 records only, not those of ws1--f1); types=parley.change.land; types=parley.change.*; types=parley.change.*,tool.started (hub and agent items); types=*; types=parley.nothing.here (expects []); session_id=S in upper case; workspace=ws1&source=agent&types=tool.*: assert ids(get('/api/v1/audit?'+query, admin).items) == expected

criteria.action: return only hub events whose field equals the value exactly, and no run event
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with hub items only

criteria.condition: `GET /api/v1/audit` is called with one of the agent-only filters `run_id`, `node_id`, `severity`, and `source` is absent or `agent`

requirements.title: The `parley audit query` command
requirements.rationale: The operator's audit starts in a shell; the command is the query with one flag per filter.

criteria.condition: a user runs `parley audit query` with any of the flags `--source`, `--workspace`, `--types`, `--session`, `--run-id`, `--actor-id`, `--resource-type`, `--resource-id`, `--action`, `--since`, `--until`, `--limit`, `--cursor`
criteria.action: send one `GET /api/v1/audit` whose query carries `source`, `workspace`, `types`, `session_id`, `run_id`, `actor_id`, `resource_type`, `resource_id`, `action`, `since`, `until`, `limit` and `cursor` for exactly the flags that were given, each value unchanged, and print the response body
criteria.contract: exit status 0; stdout holds the hub's `{items, next_cursor}` document as one JSON document; stderr is empty

requirements.title: The retention run
requirements.rationale: Retention is eleven independent clean-ups; one that fails must not leave the other ten undone, and the operator must be able to see that it failed.

criteria.contract: each step has ended before the next starts; the task returns no error when every step succeeded

criteria.contract: the step returns no error; a later `GET /sessions/:id` of such a session shows `status: timeout`; an `active` session started exactly at the cutoff or later stays `active`; terminal sessions are unchanged; no hub event is written

requirements.title: The metrics registry and its recorder
requirements.rationale: A dashboard built on a documented metric must never find it missing; and twenty packages reporting numbers must not each invent their own exposition.

criteria.action: for any of the 27 metrics of the catalogue of the PRD's Metrics section, export it from start-up, before anything was reported, under its documented name and type (counter, gauge or histogram), with one series at value 0 for every combination of its closed label values, and, for a metric with an open label (`method`, `path`, `status`, `workspace`, `model`, `type`), with the open labels set to the empty string until the metric has its first reported series
criteria.contract: a fresh registry's exposition has, per metric, one `# TYPE <name> <type>` line and at least one sample; a histogram has one `_bucket` sample per documented bucket bound plus `le="+Inf"`, a `_sum` and a `_count`, all 0

criteria.action: apply the report so that the next exposition shows it: a counter grows by the amount, a gauge takes the value, and a histogram adds the observation to every bucket whose bound is at least the value, to `+Inf`, to `_sum` and to `_count`; and stop exporting the empty-label placeholder of a metric once it has a reported series

criteria.contract: `GET /metrics` still answers HTTP 200 with all 27 metrics; the failing metric's samples are all 0; the invalid sample is absent; the next scrape calls the source again

check.pseudocode: in internal/metrics/registry_test.go, a table over source behaviours {returns an error, panics, returns {type: rebuild, status: bogus}: 1 beside a valid sample}: text = expose(reg); assert text has 27 '# TYPE' lines; for the first two assert every parley_jobqueue_depth sample == 0 and the captured log names parley_jobqueue_depth; for the third assert the valid sample is exported and no series has status 'bogus'; make the source healthy; assert the next expose shows its values

criteria.action: for any number of reports and expositions made at the same time from different goroutines, apply every report exactly once and write every exposition as a well-formed document
criteria.contract: after N concurrent `Add(…, 1)` calls on one series the series equals N; no exposition taken meanwhile fails to parse

check.pseudocode: in internal/metrics/registry_test.go, run under the race detector: 50 goroutines each call Add(parley_lands_total, {result: landed}, 1) 200 times and Observe(parley_land_attempts, {}, 1) 200 times while 5 goroutines call expose(reg) and parse it; assert no parse error; assert the final landed value == 10000 and the histogram count == 10000

requirements.title: The `/metrics` endpoint and HTTP request metrics
requirements.rationale: An operator's monitoring scrapes one URL without a credential and learns how the hub's HTTP surface behaves.

criteria.condition: any client sends `GET /metrics`, with no `Authorization` header or with any value in it
criteria.action: answer the Prometheus text exposition of all 27 metrics, in the order of the catalogue, each family with one `# HELP` line and one `# TYPE` line followed by its samples sorted by label values
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `Content-Type` of media type `text/plain` with parameter `version=0.0.4`; the body parses as Prometheus text format 0.0.4; two scrapes with no report between them differ only in the samples of the HTTP request metrics

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
check.pseudocode: in internal/metrics/handler_test.go, a table over Authorization {absent, 'Bearer garbage', a valid API key}: r = get('/metrics'); assert r.status == 200; mt, params = parse media type of r.header('Content-Type'); assert mt == 'text/plain' and params.version == '0.0.4'; fams = parse(r.body); assert names(fams) == the 27 catalogue names in catalogue order; assert each family is preceded by exactly one '# HELP' and one '# TYPE' line; assert the samples of parley_scm_requests_total are sorted by (op, result); assert a request to '/api/v1/metrics' answers 404

criteria.action: for any label value, write it in the exposition with a backslash escaped as `\\`, a double quote as `\"` and a line feed as `\n`, so that the document stays one sample per line
criteria.contract: a sample whose label value holds those characters parses back to the original value

check.pseudocode: in internal/metrics/expose_test.go, a table of model label values {'a"b', 'a\\b', 'line1<LF>line2', 'plain', 'é'}: Add(parley_agent_tokens_total, {workspace: ws1, model: v, direction: input}, 1); text = expose(reg); assert the sample occupies one line; assert parse(text) yields a series whose model label == v

criteria.condition: `parleyd` has answered an HTTP request on any route: a REST route, a git route, a webhook ingress route, `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/version` or `/metrics`
criteria.action: add 1 to `parley_http_requests_total` with `method` the request's method, `path` the path of the router pattern that matched (the route template, never the concrete URL) or `unmatched` when no pattern matched, and `status` the three-digit status that was sent, and observe the request's duration in seconds on `parley_http_request_duration_seconds` with the same `method` and `path`
criteria.contract: two requests to the same route with different path parameter values grow one series by 2; the histogram's `_count` for that `method` and `path` grows by 2

setup: a metrics registry and the instrumentation wrapped around a net/http router
a test clock fixed at 2026-06-01T12:00:00Z
check.pseudocode: in internal/metrics/http_test.go, behind the instrumentation a router with the patterns 'GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/sync', 'GET /git/{org}/{repo}/info/refs' and 'GET /healthz' and a handler that advances the test clock by 30 ms: get('/api/v1/workspaces/a/sync'); get('/api/v1/workspaces/b/sync'); get('/git/o/r.git/info/refs') answered 401; get('/healthz'); get('/no/such/path') answered 404; post('/healthz') answered 405: assert value(parley_http_requests_total{method=GET, path=/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/sync, status=200}) == 2; assert the git series has status '401' and its pattern as path; assert {method=GET, path=unmatched, status=404} == 1; assert no series has a path label containing '/a/' or 'no/such'; assert parley_http_request_duration_seconds_count{method=GET, path=/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/sync} == 2, its le=0.05 bucket == 2 and its le=0.025 bucket == 0; and in handler_test.go against the in-process hub: get('/metrics') twice; assert the second body shows parley_http_requests_total{method=GET, path=/metrics, status=200} >= 1

criteria.condition: `/metrics` is called with a method other than `GET` or `HEAD`
criteria.action: refuse the request and write no exposition
criteria.contract: HTTP 405 with an `Allow` header that names `GET`

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
check.pseudocode: in internal/metrics/handler_test.go, a table over methods {POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH}: r = request(method, '/metrics'); assert r.status == 405 and r.header('Allow') contains 'GET'; assert r.body has no '# TYPE' line

execution_paths.title: An operator audits a workspace from the shell

steps.action: ingests one run event for a run of workspace `demo` with POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/runs/:run_id/events
stores the run event; a hub event of `demo` was written earlier by the event component
runs `parley audit query --workspace demo` with the admin token
authenticates, validates the filters, reads the hub events under the visibility rule and the run events of `demo`, merges them newest first and answers the list envelope
prints the list as JSON on stdout and exits 0

real_components: the parleyd HTTP server with the conventions of package 02
authentication and the access rule of packages 04 and 07
the telemetry store and ingestion route of package 50
the event component and store of package 52
the parley CLI of internal/cli run in-process against the hub's address
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
workspace `demo` registered the way the end-to-end tests of package 10 register a workspace, which leaves at least one hub event with workspace `demo`
an agent credential with write access to `demo` and the admin token
end_state: the command exited 0 with one JSON document on stdout and nothing on stderr
the document's items hold the ingested run event with source `agent` and at least one item with source `hub`, all with workspace `demo`
the items are ordered by time descending
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/audit_test.go: post('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/runs/'+run+'/events', {event_type: 'tool.started'}, agentCred) -> 201; code = cli.Run(ctx, ['audit', 'query', '--workspace', 'demo'], stdout, stderr) with the admin token; assert code == 0 and stderr == ''; items = json(stdout).items; assert any(i.source == 'agent' and i.type == 'tool.started' and i.run_id == run); assert any(i.source == 'hub' and i.seq > 0); assert all(i.workspace == 'demo'); assert times(items) are non-increasing

execution_paths.title: A developer inspects what one node of a run did

steps.action: ingests the traces of node `coder` for one run of workspace `demo`
sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/runs/:run_id/traces with an API key
checks read access, validates the run id and answers the traces of that run in ascending (timestamp, id) order
orders the node's traces by timestamp and sequence, maps each to a role, skips session.result and answers the conversation

real_components: the parleyd HTTP server with the conventions of package 02
authentication and the access rule of packages 04 and 07
the telemetry store and ingestion routes of package 50
the per-run read routes of internal/telemetry
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
workspace `demo` owned by the developer
an agent credential with write access to `demo`
end_state: the traces list answered 200 with the four ingested traces in ascending order
the transcript answered 200 with three items whose roles are system, assistant, tool_use
nothing was written by the two reads: a second traces read answers the same body
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/audit_test.go: post four traces (session.init, assistant.message with data.content 'hello', tool.use with data.tool_name 'bash', session.result) to '/api/v1/workspaces/demo/runs/'+run+'/traces' with node_id 'coder'; t = get('.../traces', devKey); assert t.status == 200 and len(t.items) == 4 and timestamps ascend; tr = get('.../transcript?node_id=coder', devKey); assert [i.role for i in tr.items] == ['system', 'assistant', 'tool_use']; assert tr.items[1].content == 'hello' and tr.items[2].tool_name == 'bash'; assert get('.../traces', devKey).body == t.body

execution_paths.title: Retention prunes old records at start and the operator watches it on /metrics

steps.action: sets `[audit].max_age = "1d"` in the configuration file and starts `parleyd` on a data directory that holds run events older than one day
validates the retention keys, starts the maintenance loop, and runs the `retention` task right after start: the eleven steps in order
deletes the run events older than one day, recomputes the record gauges and sets `parley_retention_last_run_timestamp_seconds`
answers the text exposition of all 27 metrics, with the last-run timestamp, the record counts and the count of the scrape itself

real_components: the hub composition of package 03 with its configuration loader and maintenance loop
the transactional and analytical stores on disk
the retention run and its steps in internal/audit
the metrics registry, the HTTP instrumentation and the /metrics handler of internal/metrics
setup: a data directory in t.TempDir() prepared by a first in-process hub: workspace `demo`, one run event with a timestamp three days ago and one with a timestamp of now, ingested through the route of package 50
a configuration file with [audit] max_age = "1d"
the hub restarted in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 on the same data directory
end_state: the run event of three days ago is gone and the one of now remains, as GET …/runs/:run_id/events shows
GET /metrics answered 200 without a credential with media type text/plain and version 0.0.4
the body holds all 27 metric names
parley_retention_last_run_timestamp_seconds is greater than 0 and every parley_retention_errors_total series is 0
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/metrics_test.go: start hub 1, ingest the two run events, stop it; write config with audit.max_age '1d'; start hub 2 on the same directory; poll get('/metrics') until parley_retention_last_run_timestamp_seconds > 0 (at most 10 s); m = parse(body); assert the 27 catalogue names are all families of m; assert every parley_retention_errors_total sample == 0; assert m['parley_audit_records']{kind=run_event} == 1; ids = get('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/runs/'+run+'/events', ownerKey).items; assert ids == [the new event]; assert content type media type == 'text/plain' with version '0.0.4'
